butir.teks: An account of the harms of debate and the destructive traits of character that arise from it

Know, and be certain, that debate set up with the aim of overcoming and silencing, of displaying one's excellence and eminence, of speaking with affected eloquence before people, of boasting and quarrelling, and of turning people's faces towards oneself, is the wellspring of all the traits that are blameworthy to Allah and praiseworthy to the enemy of Allah, Iblis.

Its relation to the inner indecencies, such as arrogance (kibr), self-admiration ('ujb), envy (hasad), rivalry, self-praise, love of status, and others, is like the relation of drinking wine to the outward indecencies of fornication, slanderous accusation, killing, and theft.

Just as a man who is given a choice between drinking and the other indecencies regards drinking as slight and goes ahead with it, and that then calls him to commit the remaining indecencies in his drunkenness, so too whoever is overcome by the love of silencing and overcoming in debate, and by the seeking of status and boasting, is called by that to harbour all the vile things in the self, and it stirs up in him all the blameworthy traits.
The evidence for the condemnation of these traits, from the reports and the verses, will come in the Quarter of Destructive Matters.

But for now we point to the main categories of what debate stirs up. Among them is envy. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Envy devours good deeds as fire devours firewood." (١) The debater is never free of envy, for at times he overcomes and at times he is overcome, and at times his speech is praised and at other times another's speech is praised.

So as long as there remains in the world anyone who is mentioned together with him for strength of knowledge and reasoning, or whom he thinks to be better than him in speech and stronger in reasoning, he is bound to envy him and to love that blessings be removed from him and that hearts and faces turn away from that other person to himself.

Envy is a burning fire. Whoever is afflicted with it is in torment in this world, and the torment of the Hereafter is more severe and greater. For that reason Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said, "Take knowledge wherever you find it, and do not accept what the jurists say about one another, for they are jealous of one another as billy goats are jealous in the pen."

Among them is arrogance and exalting oneself over people. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Whoever is arrogant, Allah brings him low, and whoever is humble, Allah raises him." (٢) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, relating from Allah Most High, "Greatness is My lower garment and majesty is My cloak; whoever contends with Me over them, I will break him." (٣) The debater is never free of arrogance towards

his peers and equals, and of exalting himself above his station, so much so that they fight over a seat in a gathering, competing over it in being higher or lower, in nearness to or distance from the cushion of the place of honour, and in going first when entering at narrow places in the roads. And the dull-witted and the cunning deceiver among them may even make the excuse that he is seeking to preserve the honour of knowledge and that the believer is forbidden to humiliate himself (١), so the humility that Allah and all His prophets praised is expressed as abasement, and the arrogance that is detested by Allah as the might of religion, distorting the name and misleading people with it, just as was done with the name of wisdom and knowledge and others.
Among them is rancour, and the debater scarcely ever lacks it.
He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The believer is not rancorous." (٢) And what has been reported in condemnation of rancour is not hidden.

You will not see a debater who is able to avoid harbouring rancour against one who moves his head at the speech of the debater's opponent and hesitates over the debater's speech, and does not meet him with good listening. Rather, when he sees that, he is compelled to harbour rancour and nurture it within himself, and the utmost of his restraint is to hide it by hypocrisy, and it seeps out of him to the outside without fail in most cases.

How could he be free of this, when it is inconceivable that all the listeners agree on preferring his speech and approving of all his conduct in presenting it and delivering it? Rather, if even the slightest cause arose from his opponent showing little regard for his speech, rancour would be planted in his chest that time would never uproot, to the end of his life.

Among them is backbiting (ghiba), which Allah likened to eating carrion. The debater keeps persisting in eating carrion, for he never ceases to relate his opponent's speech and to disparage him. The utmost of his caution is that he be truthful in what he relates against him and not lie in reporting from him; so he inevitably relates about him what shows the shortcoming of his speech, his incapacity, and his lack of excellence, and that is backbiting; as for lying, it is slander. Likewise he cannot keep his tongue from attacking the honour of one who turns away from his speech and listens to his opponent and attends to him, until he attributes to him ignorance, stupidity, poor understanding, and dullness.
Among them is self-praise. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, says, ⟦QS 53:32⟧ And a sage was asked, "What is ugly truthfulness?" and he said, "A person's praise of himself."

The debater is never without praising himself for strength, victory, and precedence over his peers. In the course of the debate he never stops saying, "I am not one from whom the likes of these matters are hidden; I am versed in the sciences, self-reliant in the fundamentals and in the memorisation of hadith," and other things with which he praises himself, at times out of conceit and at times out of the need to promote his speech.

It is known that conceit and self-praise are both blameworthy by the Law and by reason. Among them is spying and tracking people's faults. Allah Most High says, ⟦QS 49:12⟧ The debater never ceases to seek the slips of his peers and to track the faults of his opponents, so much so that when he is told of a debater arriving in his town, he looks for someone who will inform him of his hidden circumstances and draws out his ugly deeds by questioning, until he counts them as a reserve for himself, to expose and shame him if need arises. He even investigates the circumstances of his boyhood and the defects of his body, hoping to stumble on a lapse or a defect in him, such as baldness or the like. Then, when he senses the slightest defeat from his side, he alludes to it if he is self-restrained, and this is deemed good of him and counted among the subtleties of contrivance; and he does not refrain from stating it openly if he is one who boasts of foolishness and mockery, as is related of some of the great debaters who are counted among their champions.

Among them is rejoicing at people's misfortune and being distressed at their joy. Whoever does not love for his Muslim brother what he loves for himself is far from the character of the believers. Everyone who seeks to boast by displaying excellence is inevitably pleased by what harms his peers and equals who vie with him in excellence, and hatred exists between them as between co-wives. Just as one co-wife, when she sees her fellow from afar, trembles in her flesh and turns pale, so too you see the debater, when he sees another debater, his colour changes and his thoughts are disturbed, as if he were beholding a rebellious devil or a ravening beast. So where is the familiarity and ease that used to exist among the scholars of religion when they met, and what has been transmitted about them of brotherhood, mutual support, and sharing in times of ease

and hardship, to the point that al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Knowledge among people of excellence and intellect is a connecting kinship." So I do not know how a group claims to follow his school when knowledge has become among them a severing enmity. Can intimacy be ascribed to them while they seek victory and boasting? Far from it, far from it! Let it suffice as an evil that it binds you to the character of hypocrites and removes you from the character of the believers and the God-fearing (taqwa).

Among them is hypocrisy, and there is no need to mention proofs of its condemnation. They are compelled to it, for they meet their opponents and those who love them and their partisans, and find no escape from showing affection to them with the tongue, expressing longing, and esteeming their standing and circumstances. The one addressed, the one addressing, and everyone who hears them know that this is falsehood, lies, hypocrisy, and wickedness, for they show affection with their tongues while bearing hatred in their hearts. We seek refuge in Allah the Great from it. He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "When people learn knowledge and abandon action, show love with their tongues and hate with their hearts, and sever family ties, Allah curses them at that time, so He makes them deaf and blinds their eyes." (١) Al-Hasan transmitted it, and it has been proven true by witnessing this condition.

Among them is arrogance towards the truth and dislike of it, and eagerness to dispute over it, so much so that the thing most hateful to the debater is that the truth appear on the tongue of his opponent. Whenever it appears, he girds himself to reject and deny it with his utmost effort, and expends all he can in deceit, scheming, and trickery to repel it, until disputing over it becomes a natural habit, so that he hears no speech except that an impulse to object to it arises from his nature, until that overcomes his heart even regarding the proofs of the Qur'an and the words of the Law, and he strikes some of them against others. And disputation set against falsehood is something to be avoided, since the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) encouraged leaving disputation with the truth against falsehood.

He (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Whoever abandons disputation while he is in the wrong, Allah builds for him a house on the outskirts of Paradise, and whoever abandons disputation while he is in the right, Allah builds for him a house in the highest part of Paradise." (٢) Allah Most High equated the one who fabricates lies against Allah with the one who denies the truth, and said, ⟦QS 29:68⟧ And Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 39:32⟧ Among them is showing off (riya'), regard for people, and effort to win over their hearts and turn their faces.

Showing off is the incurable disease that calls to the greatest of the major sins, as will come in the Book of Showing Off. The debater intends nothing but to appear before people and for their tongues to be loosed in praising him. These, then, are ten traits from the mothers of the inner indecencies, apart from what happens to those among them who lack restraint, in the form of quarrelling that leads to striking, punching, slapping, tearing garments, seizing beards, cursing parents, reviling teachers, and outright slander; for those are not counted among the people of consideration. Rather, it is the great ones and the intelligent among them who are never free of these ten traits. Yes, some of them may be spared some of these traits with someone who is clearly lower than him or clearly above him, or who is far from his own town and means of livelihood; but none of them is free of them with his peers who rank alongside him in degree.

Then from each of these ten traits there branch out ten more of the vices, which we have not lengthened by mentioning and detailing one by one, such as haughtiness, anger, hatred, greed, love of seeking wealth and status in order to be able to win and boast, exultation and insolence, exalting the wealthy and rulers, frequenting them and taking from their unlawful gains, adorning oneself with horses, mounts, and forbidden clothes, despising people out of pride and conceit, engaging in what does not concern one, much talk, the departure of awe, fear, and mercy from the heart and the dominance of heedlessness over it, until the one praying among them does not know in his prayer what he has prayed, what he is reciting, or whom he is conversing with, and feels no humility in his heart, while he spends his life in the sciences that help in debate though they do not benefit in the Hereafter, such as embellishing expression and rhyming words
and memorising anecdotes, and other matters beyond counting.

Debaters differ in these according to their ranks, and they have various ranks; yet even the greatest of them in religion and the most of them in intellect is not free of a good number of the roots of these traits. The utmost he does is conceal them and strive against the self with regard to them.

Know that these vices are also bound to anyone occupied with reminding and exhortation, if his aim is to seek acceptance, establish status, and gain wealth and might; and they are also bound to anyone occupied with the knowledge of the school and legal opinions (fatwas), if his aim is to seek the judgeship, the administration of endowments, and precedence over his peers.

In sum, they are bound to everyone who seeks through knowledge anything other than the reward of Allah Most High in the Hereafter. Knowledge does not leave the scholar be; rather it either destroys him with eternal destruction or gives him life with eternal life. For that reason he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "The most severely punished of people on the Day of Resurrection is a scholar whom Allah has not benefited by his knowledge." So it has harmed him even though it did not benefit him, and would that he had escaped from it breaking even. Far from it, far from it! The peril of knowledge is great, and its seeker seeks eternal sovereignty and everlasting bliss, so he is bound to end up with either sovereignty or perdition. He is like one who seeks kingship in this world: if he does not happen to succeed in getting wealth, he cannot hope to be safe from humiliation; rather he must inevitably remain in the most disgraceful of states. If you say, "There is a benefit in allowing debate, which is to make people eager to seek knowledge, for were it not for the love of leadership, the sciences would be effaced," you have spoken truly from one aspect, but it is of no use, for were it not for the promise of the ball, the polo stick, and playing with sparrows, boys would not be eager to go to school, and that does not show that eagerness for it is praiseworthy; and were it not for the love of leadership, knowledge would be effaced.

And that does not show that the seeker of leadership is saved; rather he is among those about whom he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Allah will support this religion with people who have no share." (١) And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "Allah will support this religion with the wicked man." (٢) The seeker of leadership is in himself ruined, though others may be set right because of him, if he calls to abandoning this world; and that applies to one whose outward state, on the face of it, is the outward state of the scholars of the early generations (salaf), but who harbours the intention of status. His likeness is that of the candle that burns itself while others are lit by it, so the good of others lies in his destruction. But if he calls to seeking this world, his likeness is that of the burning fire that consumes itself and others.

The scholars are three: one who destroys himself and others, namely those who openly declare for seeking this world and turn towards it; one who brings felicity to himself and others, namely those who call people to Allah, glorified and exalted is He, outwardly and inwardly; and one who destroys himself and brings felicity to others, namely he who calls to the Hereafter and has outwardly abandoned this world, while his intention inwardly is acceptance by people and the establishing of status. So look at which of these categories you are, and for whom you have occupied yourself with taking account. Do not think that Allah Most High accepts any knowledge or action other than what is purely for His face.
In the Book of Showing Off, indeed in the whole Quarter of Destructive Matters, there will come to you what removes doubt about it from you, if Allah Most High wills.
